title: Subquadratic exact fully dynamic weighted single-source distances
formal: Do a constant \(\delta>0\) and a deterministic data structure exist that maintain exact distances from one fixed source in every fully dynamic undirected \(n\)-vertex graph with positive integer edge weights at most \(n^3\), using polynomial preprocessing and space, \(O(n^{2-\delta})\) worst-case update time and \(O(1)\) worst-case time per distance query in the word-RAM model below?

source_formulation.text: That is, we do not know how to do better than reconstructing from scratch after every edge update.
source_formulation.caption: Complete selected source sentence; PDF p. 2

why: Dynamic shortest paths asks how much computation can be reused as a network changes. Separating update cost, query cost, approximation and graph density is essential to deciding whether a data structure meaningfully improves on a static computation.
status_note: The 2017 blanket rebuilding remark is obsolete for several variants. This user-authorized exact weighted variant was specified on 13 September 2026; the checked later sources separate it from approximate and unweighted results. Their conditional barriers are not an unconditional resolution, and no exact new theorem for the selected model was identified in the bounded search.

progress.text: The original introduction gives rebuilding as the general fully dynamic baseline.
The later approximate-distance result beats that baseline in weighted dense settings, but does not maintain the exact distances selected here.

importance.reason: A fundamental reuse-of-computation question for changing networks, whose precise remaining significance depends on accuracy, weights, density and query guarantees. Existing score retained.

sentences: The data structure maintains exact distances from a fixed source while weighted edges are inserted, removed or changed.
Every individual distance query must take constant time.
The selected target is a fixed polynomial saving below quadratic worst-case update time in the vertex count.
Weights are positive integers of explicitly bounded size and all computation is charged on a specified word-RAM.
Known approximate and unweighted improvements do not settle this exact weighted variant.

definitions: The vertex set is \([n]\), with \(n\ge2\), and the source \(s\in[n]\) is fixed at initialization. Graphs are simple and undirected. Every present edge has an integer weight in \(\{1,\ldots,n^3\}\). An update inserts an absent edge with its weight, deletes a present edge, or changes the weight of a present edge. A query supplies \(v\in[n]\) and must return exactly the minimum sum of edge weights along an \(s\)-to-\(v\) path in the current graph, or a special infinity symbol if no path exists; the distance to \(s\) is zero. Each operation must finish before the next is supplied. The sequence may be arbitrarily long and chosen using all previous outputs; the data structure receives no future operations. It must work at every density. The subquadratic bound is in the vertex count, so it expresses a saving over rebuilding for dense graphs, not a promised saving relative to the edge count of every sparse graph. The uniform machine is a word-RAM with word length \(w=c\lceil\log_2(n+2)\rceil\), for one fixed integer \(c\ge5\) chosen with the algorithm. Unit-cost instructions are indirect read/write of an addressed word, comparison, branching, unsigned addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^w\), bitwise Boolean operations, shifts by fewer than \(w\) places, and integer quotient/remainder by a nonzero word. Larger integers require multiple words and charged operations. Initial input is an explicit adjacency/weight table. For fixed constants \(K,C\), initialization takes at most \(Cn^K\) operations and at most \(Cn^K\) words are stored at any time, with addresses fitting the word length. Each individual update takes at most \(Cn^{2-\delta}\) operations and each query at most \(C\), after enlarging constants for small \(n\). The program, constants and \(\delta\) are independent of \(n\), weights and the operation sequence. The machine has no randomization, nonuniform advice or unit-cost unbounded-precision arithmetic. A path certificate is not required.
answer_criterion: Provide a Lean proof constructing the specified exact data structure with all worst-case bounds, or a Lean proof that none exists. A conditional lower bound is relevant context but does not establish unconditional nonexistence. Approximate distances, an unweighted-only result, amortized updates or nonconstant single-distance queries would change the selected target.

context_blocks.text: The 2017 introduction asks about fully dynamic single-source distances beyond rebuilding, without choosing one complete resource and accuracy profile.

The authorized variant selects exact polynomially bounded integer weights, deterministic worst-case updates and constant-time distance queries. Later approximate and unweighted improvements are retained as progress rather than repeated as unresolved tasks.

The 2023 paper distinguishes its unweighted algorithm from the weighted setting, where it cites a conditional barrier to subquadratic updates. This card asks the unconditional existence question in its explicitly fixed model.

notes: User authorized concrete variants on 13 September 2026. Selected exact undirected positive-integer distances with weights at most n^3, deterministic subquadratic worst-case updates and constant-time queries.

Defined the full online operation contract, fixed source, polynomial initialization/space, finite-word instruction set and vertex-count bound without claiming an all-density improvement relative to rebuilding.
Read the 2023 weighted-versus-unweighted discussion. Retained its conditional weighted barrier as context and did not claim that it proves unconditional nonexistence for the selected weight range.
